unit.title: Doing right because it is right
unit.needIt: A shopkeeper who is honest only so customers come back is one bad day from cheating. Kant asks what your reason is, because reasons are what last.
unit.why: Imagine you help a friend move houses. You do it because you believe in being a helpful person, not because you want them to owe you a favor later. Kant argues that your help is only truly 'good' because of your inner motive, not the move itself.
unit.outcome: Evaluate your own actions based on your underlying principles rather than just the final results.
unit.reachesYou: You see this when you choose to be honest at work even if it costs you a sale. You feel it when you help a stranger because it is the right thing to do, not for a reward.
unit.do: Identify one thing you do out of habit or self-interest this week and try to do it once purely because it is the right thing to do.

quiz.q: What does Mill say is the heart of the utilitarian view?
quiz.why: Mill argues that actions are right in proportion as they promote happiness.
quiz.quote: The first thing that he says is that he articulates what's known as the greatest happiness principle.

quiz.q: According to Mill, what is irrelevant to an act's moral worth?
quiz.why: Mill states that the motive has nothing to do with the morality of the action.
quiz.quote: He says, the motive has nothing to do with the morality of the action.

quiz.q: In the Jim case, what did most people think Jim should do?
quiz.why: Most people in the lecture chose to shoot one person to save nineteen.
quiz.quote: almost three-quarters of you, actually more than three-quarters of you, think that what the morally right thing for Jim to do in this case is to shoot one man, thereby liberating the other nineteen?

quiz.q: What does Kant say about talents like intelligence or courage?
choices: They are better than a good will
They are only good if part of a good will
They are not useful for morality
quiz.why: Kant argues that these qualities only help you achieve goals but do not determine if those goals are good.
quiz.quote: Each of the virtues that has traditionally been extolled as a virtue, says Kant, gains its value only in so far as the goodwill is part of it.

quiz.q: What is a 'good will' according to Kant?
quiz.why: Kant believes a good will is good in itself, regardless of what it accomplishes.
quiz.quote: Now, a goodwill, says Kant, is good not because of what it affects or accomplishes. It's good in itself.

quiz.q: What is the Kantian notion of 'duty'?
quiz.why: Kant defines duty as the necessity of an action done out of respect for the law.
quiz.quote: duty is the necessity of an action done out of the respect for the law.

quiz.q: How does Kant view an act done out of self-interest?
quiz.why: Kant believes that for an act to have moral worth, it must be done from duty, not for personal gain.
quiz.quote: If you obey the law, but you do so only out of self-interest, your obedience, says Kant, has no moral worth.

beats.say: One is honest because it is good for business.

For Kant an act has moral worth only when done from duty.

line.label: Kant: the worth is in the will, not the result.

partials: The outcome of an act does not determine its moral worth.
A good will is good in itself.
Actions must be done from duty to have moral worth.
A maxim is the description of an act.
Duty is respect for the moral law.
crystal.key: Moral worth comes from the intent and the principle behind an action, not the result.

decoys.text: A good act is one that makes the most people happy.
decoys.why: This is utilitarianism, which Kant criticizes.

decoys.text: Doing something because you enjoy it is a moral act.
decoys.why: Kant says acting from inclination, not duty, has no moral worth.

crystal.aha: When you move from looking at what happened to why you did it, you find Kant's focus on the good will.
